Tommy told his mom about the owl and then the three of them said goodbye to the owl and rushed home together.

Sara and Sam were twins. They liked to play in the park with their dog, Spot. Spot was a big, brown dog who could run very fast and catch a ball. Sara and Sam could whistle, and they taught Spot to come when they whistled.

One day, they went to the park with their mom. The park was very busy. There were many kids and dogs and bikes and kites. Sara and Sam wanted to play with Spot, but they had to be careful not to lose him. They put a red collar on him, so they could see him better.

"Spot, stay close to us," Sara said. "We don't want you to get lost."

"Whistle if you can't find him," Sam said. "He will hear you and come back."

They threw the ball for Spot, and he ran after it. He was very happy. He liked to play with Sara and Sam. They whistled and he came back. They did this many times.

But then, something bad happened. A big, black dog ran into the park. He saw Spot and wanted to play with him. He barked and chased Spot. Spot was scared. He ran away from the big, black dog. He ran so far that he could not see Sara and Sam anymore.

"Sara, where is Spot?" Sam asked. He looked around, but he could not see him.

"I don't know, Sam. He was here a minute ago," Sara said. She was worried. She looked around, but she could not see him either.

They started to whistle. They whistled very loud. They hoped that Spot would hear them and come back. But Spot did not come back. He was lost.

Once upon a time, there was a person named Tim. Tim liked to fly kites on sunny days. One day, Tim went to the park to fly his kite. But, when he got there, he saw that his kite was broken. Tim was upset because he couldn't fly his kite. 

Suddenly, Tim saw a butterfly flying in the sky. He watched the butterfly flutter up and down, and it made him feel happy. Tim realized that he didn't need a kite to fly, he could just watch the butterfly. So, he sat down on the grass and watched the butterfly fly up and down. 

After a while, Tim saw a bird flying high in the sky. He thought it was amazing how the bird could fly so high. Tim wanted to fly like the bird, but he knew he couldn't. Instead, he decided to go home and draw a picture of the bird flying. Tim was no longer upset about his broken kite, he was happy just watching things fly.

Little Jimmy was a naughty boy. He liked to do things he wasn't supposed to. His mom and dad reminded him every day to be nice, but he didn't listen and kept getting into trouble.

One day, Jimmy was playing outside and got very, very wet. His mom was so mad and said, "Jimmy, I told you to bring a towel with you, but you were naughty and forgot it." Jimmy just shrugged and said he didn't care.

His mom was so angry that she told him to stay outside until he dried off. Jimmy protested, but his mom and dad wouldn't budge. Jimmy stayed outside until he was all dry, shivering in the cold.

When Jimmy came back to the house, his mom said, "You see, Jimmy, this is why it's important to listen. You should never be naughty or forget what your parents tell you!" But Jimmy refused to listen. In the end, Jimmy had to stay outside for the rest of the day, and his parents were never able to remind him to be nicer again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the store with her mommy. They picked out some yummy snacks and went to the cashier. The cashier said, "That will be five dollars, please." 

Lily's mommy gave the cashier some money, and the cashier gave them their snacks. Lily looked up at her mommy and said, "Mommy, can I pay next time?" 

Her mommy smiled and said, "Of course, sweetie." Lily was so grateful that her mommy said yes. 

As they walked out of the store, Lily held her mommy's hand and said, "Thank you for letting me pay next time, mommy. I love you." Her mommy gave her a big hug and said, "I love you too, Lily."

Once upon a time there lived a little boy, Kevin. He was three years old and he wanted to be independent. One sunny day his mom suggested he try to manage on his own. But Kevin was afraid that he wouldn't be able to do it. 

"Mom, I don't think I can manage," Kevin told his mom. 

"Oh come on, it won't be that difficult," his mom said, smiling. She showed him a spot in the garden that she wanted him to clean. 

"Okay, I'll try," Kevin said, determined. He worked hard, and eventually he managed to clean up the spot. 

The next day, his mom suggested he try again. But this time the spot was twice as big. He was worried he wouldn't be able to do it. 

But Kevin remembered how he managed the day before and he refused to give up. He worked hard and eventually he managed to clean the spot again. Kevin felt proud of himself for being independent and managing on his own.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sarah. She was only three and loved to do things. One day, when she was out in the garden, she saw something shiny. It was a coin! It was different to any other coin Sarah had seen before. She picked it up and looked at it. What could she do with it? Suddenly, Sarah got an idea. She ran to her mum and showed her the coin. She asked her mum if they could go to the shop and buy some sweets with it. Her mum said yes, and they set off together. 

When they arrived at the shop, Sarah put the coin in the red machine. The machine made a noise and then gave her some sweets. Sarah was so excited and couldn't wait to eat them. On their way home, Sarah and her mum talked about all the different things you can do with a coin. 

Sarah was so happy to have found such a nice coin. She thanked her mum for taking her to the shop. From that day on, Sarah was always on the lookout for different coins!

Once upon a time, there was a kind bear named Benny. Benny lived in a big forest with his animal friends. One day, Benny saw a little bird who was very sad. 

"What's wrong?" asked Benny in a compassionate voice. 

"I lost my way home," the bird said with a sad chirp. 

"Don't worry," said Benny. "I can help you find your way. Let's weigh your options." 

Benny picked up the little bird and held him gently in his big paws. He looked up at the sun in the sky and used his keen sense of direction to lead the bird back to his home. 

"Thank you, Benny!" chirped the little bird happily as he flew into his nest. Benny smiled and waved goodbye, happy to have helped his friend find his way home.

name_of_work: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell by William Blake
content: Rintrah roars and shakes his fires in the burdened air; Hungry clouds swag on the deep. Once meek, and in a perilous path, The just man kept his course along The vale of death. Roses are planted where thorns grow, And on the barren heath Sing the honey bees. Then the perilous path was planted: And a river and a spring On every cliff and tomb; And on the bleached bones Red clay brought forth. Till the villain left the paths of ease, To walk in perilous paths, and drive The just man into barren climes. Now the sneaking serpent walks In mild humility, And the just man rages in the wilds Where lions roam. Rintrah roars and shakes his fires in the burdened air; Hungry clouds swag on the deep.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog. The dog had an owner. The owner loved the dog. One day, the owner and the dog went for a walk. They went to a big park. The park had many trees and flowers. The owner saw a hidden spot behind a big tree. The owner wanted to sit there.

The owner said to the dog, "Sit here with me." The owner sat down with the dog. The owner did not attach the dog to a leash. The dog saw a squirrel. The squirrel was running and playing. The dog wanted to play too. The dog ran after the squirrel. The owner called the dog, but the dog did not come back.

The owner looked for the dog. The owner called the dog's name. The dog did not hear the owner. The dog was lost. The owner was sad. The dog was sad too. They could not find each other. The owner went home without the dog. The dog stayed in the park. The dog and the owner did not have a happy ending.

Once upon a time, there was a purple bulb who loved to scatter. He would jump high into the air and then throw his petals every which way. The petals from the purple bulb twirled and danced, filling the air with color. Everyone who saw him was filled with joy.

One day, the purple bulb felt a strong wind. He held on tight and the wind scattered him even further! He flew over farms and streets, until the wind finally stopped. 

When the purple bulb landed, he was in a big, green garden. He was excited to discover he was surrounded by so many different colored bulbs - yellow, pink and blue. 

The purple bulb was so happy to be in such a beautiful place. He scattered his petals with even more enthusiasm and joy. From that day on, the purple bulb and his friends scattered together, filling the garden with life and love.

Dream-singers, Story-tellers, Dancers, Loud laughers in the hands of Fate-- My People. Dish-washers, Elevator-boys, Ladies' maids, Crap-shooters, Cooks, Waiters, Jazzers, Nurses of babies, Loaders of ships, Porters, Hairdressers, Comedians in vaudeville And band-men in circuses-- Dream-singers all, Story-tellers all. Dancers-- God! What dancers! Singers-- God! What singers! Singers and dancers, Dancers and laughers. Laughers? Yes, laughers....laughers.....laughers-- Loud-mouthed laughers in the hands of Fate.

Once upon a time, there was a thick chicken. It liked to dance around the farm and talk to the other animals. One day, the chicken was walking around the barn when it noticed a small mouse.

The chicken stopped and asked, "Are you ok?" 
The mouse replied, "Yes, I am ok, but I need to find someone to teach me the dance steps." 

The chicken smiled, "I can help. I'm the best dancer on the farm and I know all the steps. Let's practice together!"

The mouse was very happy and followed the chicken around the barn. The chicken talked and taught the mouse each step of the dance. After a few hours, the mouse was a pro and danced as well as the chicken! 

The mouse and the chicken were now great friends and danced together every day.

We stood by a pond that winter day, And the sun was white, as though chidden of God, And a few leaves lay on the starving sod; - They had fallen from an ash, and were gray. Your eyes on me were as eyes that rove Over tedious riddles of years ago; And some words played between us to and fro On which lost the more by our love. The smile on your mouth was the deadest thing Alive enough to have strength to die; And a grin of bitterness swept thereby Like an ominous bird a-wing.... Since then, keen lessons that love deceives, And wrings with wrong, have shaped to me Your face, and the God curst sun, and a tree, And a pond edged with grayish leaves.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to try new things. One day, he saw a firework in the sky. It was big and bright. Spot wanted to see it up close.

Spot ran and ran to find the firework. He ran so far that he became tired. But he did not give up. He kept trying to find the firework. Spot knew that if he tried hard enough, he would find it.

Finally, Spot found the firework. It was on the ground, all done making pretty lights. Spot was very happy that he tried so hard to find it. He knew that trying his best was important. Spot went home, still tired but very proud of himself.

Once upon a time there was a little girl name Abbie. She was so happy and grateful for a special basket her Grandma had given her. 

Abbie held the basket tight as she looked inside. The basket was so beautiful and it glowed in the sunlight! In the basket was lots of things she loved. There were her favortie stuffed animal and treats! 

She was so excited that she ran outside with her basket. Abbie went to show her friends and they were all so happy. Her friends wanted to play with the things in Abbie's basket. 

Abbie was so grateful that she shared her special basket with her friends. They all played for hours with their new toys and treats. And Abbie was so happy that the basket glowed brighter than ever before. 

The End.

name_of_work: Flying Inside Your Own Body by Margaret Atwood
content: Your lungs fill & spread themselves, wings of pink blood, and your bones empty themselves and become hollow. When you breathe in you'll lift like a balloon and your heart is light too & huge, beating with pure joy, pure helium. The sun's white winds blow through you, there's nothing above you, you see the earth now as an oval jewel, radiant & seablue with love. It's only in dreams you can do this. Waking, your heart is a shaken fist, a fine dust clogs the air you breathe in; the sun's a hot copper weight pressing straight down on the think pink rind of your skull. It's always the moment just before gunshot. You try & try to rise but you cannot.

Once upon a time, there lived a nation of people who all loved each other very much. They cared for each other in the most adorable ways. Every morning they would do very kind things, like bringing each other breakfast in bed.

They also liked to do fun activities together, like playing with balloons and doing races around the park. Everyone had fun and made lots of memories that would last forever.

At the end of each day, they all held hands and danced in a big circle. It was such a happy time! Everyone smiled and laughed with joy. 

The people in this nation were very lucky to have each other. They showed love in every adorable way and were a family like no other.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his dad. They saw a peaceful lake with ducks swimming in it. Tim wanted to play golf with his dad by the lake. His dad said, "Okay, let's play!"

Tim found a small stick and his dad found a big one. They used the sticks to hit a small ball. "I love golf!" Tim said, laughing. They played and played until the sun went down.

When they got home, Tim's mom asked, "Did you have fun?" Tim said, "Yes, we played golf by the peaceful lake!" His mom smiled and said, "Now, let's polish our shoes before bedtime." So, Tim and his dad cleaned their shoes together. They all had a very happy day.

name_of_work: Wild With All Regrets by Wilfred Owen
content: To Siegfried Sassoon My arms have mutinied against me--brutes! My fingers fidget like ten idle brats, My back's been stiff for hours, damned hours. Death never gives his squad a Stand-at-ease. I can't read. There: it's no use. Take you book. A short life and a merry one, my buck! We said we'd hate to grow dead old. But now, Not to live old seems awful: not to renew My boyhood with my boys, and teach 'em hitting, Shooting and hunting,--all the arts of hurting! --Well, that's what I learnt. That, and making money. your fifty years in store seem none too many; But I've five minutes. God! For just two years To help myself to this good air of yours! One Spring! Is one too hard to spare? Too long? Spring air would find its own way to my lung, And grow me legs as quick as lilac-shoots. Yes, there's the orderly. He'll change the sheets When I'm lugged out, oh, couldn't I do that? Here in this coffin of a bed, I've though I'd like to kneel and sweep his floors for ever,-- And ask no nights off when the bustle's over, For I'd enjoy the dirt; who's prejudiced Against a grimed hand when his own's quite dust,-- Less live than specks that in the sun-shafts turn? Dear dust,--in rooms, on roads, on faces' tan! I'd love to be a sweep's boy, black as Town; Yes, or a muckman. Must I be his load? A flea would do. If one chap wasn't bloody, Or went stone-cold, I'd find another body. Which I shan't manage now. Unless it's yours. I shall stay in you, friend, for some few hours. You'll feel my heavy spirit chill your chest, And climb your throat on sobs, until it's chased On sighs, and wiped from off your lips by wind. I think on your rich breathing, brother, I'll be weaned To do without what blood remained me from my wound.

Anna and her mom went to the store. Anna liked the store. She saw many things. She saw toys and books and clothes. She saw a big cake. The cake was sweet. Anna wanted the cake.

"Mom, can I have the cake?" Anna asked.

"No, Anna, we have to go home. We have no money for the cake," mom said.

"But I want the cake. It is sweet. Please, mom, please," Anna said.

"Anna, stop. You have to stay with me. Do not run away. The store is big. You can get lost," mom said.

Anna did not listen. She ran away from mom. She ran to the cake. She tried to grab the cake. But the cake was too high. Anna fell down. She hurt her knee. She cried.

"Anna, where are you?" mom called.

Anna heard mom. She was scared. She wanted mom. She said, "Mom, I am here. I am sorry. I fell down. I hurt my knee. I want you."

Mom found Anna. She hugged Anna. She said, "Anna, I am here. I am sorry. You are hurt. I love you."

Mom took Anna to the car. She gave Anna a band-aid. She gave Anna a kiss. She said, "Anna, next time, you have to stay with me. Do not run away. The store is not for cake. The store is for shopping. We can make a cake at home. It will be sweet. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will stay with you. I love you. Can we make a cake at home?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Yes, Anna. We can make a cake at home. It will be fun. It will be sweet. You are my sweet girl."

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Jack. He liked going to the park and playing with his friends.

One day while Jack was at the park he saw a big tree with lots of fruit hanging from it. He was excited - it looked like it had lots of delicious fruit! He wanted to take some with him for a snack.
 
Jack grabbed as many fruits as he could, but he lifted too hard and some of them fell on the ground. He felt embarrassed so he quickly put the fruit back on the tree and ran away.

Jack felt ashamed. He knew he shouldn't have taken the fruit without asking the tree first. He was sad that he made a mistake and he knew he had to make things right. 

So the next day, Jack brought a basket of fruit to the park and gave it to the tree. He apologized to the tree and thanked it for the fruit. The tree was happy and smiled at Jack.

Jack felt better now. He realized that he had to take responsibility for what he had done and that apologizing was the right thing to do. He vowed to never take anything from the tree again without asking first.

Once there was a brave little girl. She had bright clothes and loved to explore. One day, she went to the park by herself.

At the park, she saw many new things. She saw tall trees and small bugs. She saw green grass and blue skies. She pointed to everything, excitedly.

Then, she saw something shining in the distance. It looked like something special. She was very brave and walked closer to it.

When she got there, she saw it was a small pond. It was sparkly in the sunlight and had ducks swimming happily. She pointed to them, excitedly. 

The brave little girl made some new friends that day. She gave them pieces of her bright clothes, so they could always remember her. 

The brave little girl was excited to come back to the park soon. She will always remember the special pond she found, and how brave she was to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Tilly. She liked to bathe in the river and pretend she could swim. One day, when she was bathing, she found a broken triangle in the water. She couldn't understand why anyone would throw such a strange thing in the river.

Tilly decided to take the triangle home with her so she could have a closer look. When she got back, she looked at the triangle closely, but it was so broken, she still couldn't figure out what it was. 

Tilly wanted to keep the triangle safe, so she put it up high. But a few days later when she went to look for it, it was gone! Instead, she found the broken triangle pieces scattered all over the ground!

Tilly was sad and disappointed, she had so wanted to find out what the triangle was. Now, it was completely ruined and she could never figure out what it was. 

Tilly had lost her broken triangle.

Jill was a girl who liked to eat. She ate a lot of food every day. She ate more food than her brother Jack and her sister Jane. She ate more food than her mom and dad. She ate more food than her dog Spot.

One day, Jill saw a big plate of cookies on the table. She wanted to eat all the cookies. She did not want to share with anyone. She did not listen to her mom, who said, "Jill, leave some cookies for the others. Too many cookies are bad for you."

Jill took the plate of cookies and ran to her room. She locked the door and ate all the cookies. She ate them very fast. She did not enjoy them. She only wanted to have them all.

Soon, Jill felt sick. Her tummy hurt. She felt hot and cold. She felt dizzy and tired. She wanted to throw up. She hoped she would feel better soon. But she did not.

Her mom knocked on the door and asked, "Jill, are you okay?" Jill did not answer. She was too sick. Her mom opened the door with a key and saw Jill on the bed. She saw the empty plate of cookies. She saw Jill's pale face. She was very worried.

She called the doctor and said, "Please come quickly. My daughter ate too many cookies and now she is very sick." The doctor came and checked Jill. He said, "She has a fever and a stomach ache. She needs to go to the hospital. She may have to stay there for a long time."

Jill was scared. She did not want to go to the hospital. She did not want to leave her mom and dad and her brother and sister and her dog Spot. She wished she had not eaten all the cookies. She wished she had shared with the others. She wished she had listened to her mom. She learned a hard lesson. She learned that being greedy is bad and being kind is good. She learned that too much of anything is not good for you. She learned that she should hope for the right things and not the wrong things.

Tom was a lazy cat. He liked to sleep all day on the sofa. He did not like to play with his toys or run after mice. He only woke up when he was hungry or thirsty.

One day, Tom saw a string on the floor. It was red and shiny and long. Tom felt curious. He wanted to touch the string. He got off the sofa and walked slowly to the string.

But when he got close, the string moved. It went under the table and then out again. Tom was surprised. He followed the string with his eyes. He wanted to catch it.

The string moved again. It went up the stairs and then down again. Tom was excited. He ran after the string. He tried to jump on it and bite it.

But the string was too fast. It went into a room and then out again. Tom was tired. He stopped and panted.

Then he saw who was holding the string. It was Lily, his little human friend. She was laughing and smiling. She had been playing with Tom all along.

Tom felt happy. He liked Lily. He ran to her and rubbed his head on her leg. Lily hugged him and said, "Good boy, Tom. You are not so lazy after all. You are a fun cat. Do you want to play some more?"

Tom nodded and purred. He liked to play with Lily and the string. He forgot about the sofa and the sleep. He had a new game and a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake with her mommy. One day, they decided to make brownies.

Lily's mommy said, "Can you measure the flour for me, Lily?" Lily nodded and got the measuring cup. She filled it up and poured it in the bowl.

After they mixed all the ingredients, Lily's mommy said, "Let's wipe the counter clean." Lily grabbed a cloth and wiped the crumbs away.

When the brownies were done, they smelled so good! Lily's daddy came in and said, "Wow, those brownies look delicious!" Lily's mommy said, "We made them together. Lily measured the flour and wiped the counter clean." Lily felt proud of herself and smiled.

Tim and Lily were playing in the bathroom. They liked to splash water in the tub and make bubbles with the soap. They also liked to put toys in the water and pretend they were boats or fish.

One day, Tim had a new toy. It was a red car that could go very fast. He wanted to show Lily how fast it could go in the water. He said, "Look, Lily, this is my new car. It can go faster than any of your toys. Watch this!"

He put the car in the water and pushed a button. The car zoomed across the tub and hit the drain. The drain was open and the car went inside. Tim and Lily heard a clunk and then nothing.

Tim was very sad. He cried, "My car! My car! It went in the drain! I want it back!"

Lily was scared. She said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I didn't know the drain was open. Maybe we can get it back. Let's ask Mommy."

They ran out of the bathroom and looked for Mommy. They found her in the kitchen. She was busy making dinner. She saw them and said, "What's wrong, kids? Why are you wet and crying?"

Tim and Lily told her what happened. They said, "Mommy, Mommy, we were playing in the tub and Tim's new car went in the drain. Can you get it back for us? Please, please, please!"

Mommy was angry. She said, "You were playing in the tub without me? That's very dangerous. You could have drowned or slipped or hurt yourself. And you wasted water and soap and made a mess. And you lost Tim's new car in the drain. That's very ignorant. You should know better. You are both in big trouble. Go to your rooms right now. No dinner for you. And no more toys for a week."

Tim and Lily felt very bad. They said, "We're sorry, Mommy. We didn't mean to. We just wanted to have fun. Please don't be mad at us. Please don't send us to our rooms. Please don't take away our toys."

But Mommy didn't listen. She said, "Go now. And don't come out until I say so. And don't expect me to get your car back. It's gone forever. Maybe that will teach you a lesson."

Tim and Lily went to their rooms. They cried and cried. They wished they had never played in the tub. They wished they had never seen the car. They wished Mommy would forgive them. But she didn't. She was too busy and too angry. She forgot about them and their car. She was ignorant too.

Anna likes to play with her hair. She has long, brown hair that she can make into different styles. Sometimes she makes a ponytail, sometimes she makes braids, sometimes she makes a bun. She likes to look at herself in the mirror and see how she looks.

One day, Anna decides to try a new style. She asks her mom to help her. Her mom says, "OK, what do you want to do?" Anna says, "I want to cut my hair and make it short and curly." Her mom says, "Are you sure? That is a big change. You might miss your long hair." Anna says, "No, I want to try something new. Please, mom, please."

Her mom agrees and takes her to the salon. There, a nice lady cuts Anna's hair with scissors and makes it curly with a machine. Anna feels the machine is hot and tickles her hair. She giggles and says, "It feels funny." The lady says, "Don't worry, it will be over soon. You will look very pretty."

When the lady is done, she blows Anna's hair with a dryer. The dryer makes a loud noise and makes Anna's hair dry and fluffy. Anna says, "Wow, my hair is so different. I like it." The lady says, "You're welcome. You have a very cute style." She gives Anna a mirror and Anna sees herself. She smiles and says, "Thank you, lady. I love my new hair."

Anna goes back to her mom and shows her her new style. Her mom says, "You look very beautiful, Anna. I'm glad you like it." Anna says, "Thank you, mom. You are the best." She hugs her mom and they go home. Anna can't wait to show her new style to her friends and family. She thinks she is very brave and cool. She is happy with her new hair.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. She was very brave - but also very scared.

One day, Daisy's parents took her to the library. She opened the door and saw a huge walls of books. She was amazed!

Daisy's mum asked her, "Shall we look for a book, Daisy?" Daisy nodded, so they both went over to the bookshelf. 

Daisy looked for a bit, but then started to feel scared again. "I can't find one," she said.

Then Daisy's mum said, "Don't worry, Daisy! I have one I can recommend". She went and fetched a big book. Daisy wasn't scared any more - she was so excited to read it!

Once upon a time, there was a nice lady. She had a pretty dress and a beautiful smile. She loved pizza. She had a special pizza just for today.

The lady touched the pizza. It felt nice and warm. She took a bite and it was delicious! She smiled and said "this is the best pizza ever!"

Next, the lady wanted to make something special. She touched the pretty flowers in her garden. She said "These are so pretty, I'm going to make a bouquet to give to someone special!"

The lady gave the pizza and the pretty flowers to her neighbor. They both smiled and said "Thank you. This was so thoughtful of you." 

The lady was happy to share her pizza and pretty flowers. She knew it made them feel special, and that was all she wanted.

I never turned anyone into a pig. Some people are pigs; I make them Look like pigs. I'm sick of your world That lets the outside disguise the inside. Your men weren't bad men; Undisciplined life Did that to them. As pigs, Under the care of Me and my ladies, they Sweetened right up. Then I reversed the spell, showing you my goodness As well as my power. I saw We could be happy here, As men and women are When their needs are simple. In the same breath, I foresaw your departure, Your men with my help braving The crying and pounding sea. You think A few tears upset me? My friend, Every sorceress is A pragmatist at heart; nobody sees essence who can't Face limitation. If I wanted only to hold you I could hold you prisoner.

Once upon a time, there was a little piggy named Peppa. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Peppa and her friends decided to build a house out of bricks. It was easy to stack the bricks one on top of the other. 

But then, the wind started to blow and it got very cold. Peppa started to shiver and her friends did too. They realized that their brick house wasn't warm enough. So, they decided to build a fire inside to keep them warm. 

They gathered some sticks and lit a fire. Soon, they were all warm and cozy inside their brick house. Peppa was so happy that they found an easy solution to their problem. From then on, they always made sure to have a fire when it got cold outside. The end.

Once there was a little girl called Sophie. Sophie loved to play outside with her furry orange cat, Puss. Every day, Puss would run around in the garden and play with Sophie. Sophie would always use the garden hose to cool Puss off during summer days.

One day after lunch, Sophie took the hose out to give Puss a cool drink. Puss didn't like how the water felt coming out of the hose â€“ it felt cold and wet. Puss hated it.

Sophie said, "Puss, why do you hate the hose so much?"

Puss rubbed himself against Sophie's leg and said, "It is cold, wet and makes a funny noise. It also tickles my furry fur."

Sophie laughed and said, "Come on Puss, let's go find something else to do!"

Once upon a time there was an oyster who lived in the sea. She was an independent oyster who liked to do things her own way.

One day, the oyster left her home and ventured to a new place. She was excited to try something new and see what happened. She explored the new reef and encountered several other sea creatures.

The oyster got to know the creatures, and soon she found that the reef was full of tasty treats. She wanted to try them all, so she worked hard to search the reef for more.

The oyster was persistent and soon her efforts began to yield results! She found lots of delicious things that she hadn't seen before. She gathered them all in her shell and returned home, happy and full.

The oyster had discovered a treasure trove of goodies and was proud of her independence and all her hard work. She would come back to the reef every day, yielding something new each time!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her blocks and make a big stack. One day, while she was playing, she felt a tickle in her nose. She knew what was coming - a sneeze! 

Lily tried to hold it in, but it was too strong. She sneezed and her big stack of blocks fell down. She felt sad, but then she heard a noise. It was her dog, Max. He was barking and jumping up and down. He was alert because he heard the sneeze and wanted to make sure Lily was okay. 

Lily smiled and hugged Max. She knew that even though her blocks fell down, she still had her best friend to make her feel better. From that day on, Lily made sure to cover her nose when she felt a sneeze coming, so her blocks wouldn't fall down again.

Thou hast nor youth nor age But as it were an after dinner sleep Dreaming of both. Here I am, an old man in a dry month, Being read to by a boy, waiting for rain. I was neither at the hot gates Nor fought in the warm rain Nor knee deep in the salt marsh, heaving a cutlass, Bitten by flies, fought. My house is a decayed house, And the Jew squats on the window sill, the owner, Spawned in some estaminet of Antwerp, Blistered in Brussels, patched and peeled in London. The goat coughs at night in the field overhead; Rocks, moss, stonecrop, iron, merds. The woman keeps the kitchen, makes tea, Sneezes at evening, poking the peevish gutter. I an old man, A dull head among windy spaces. Signs are taken for wonders. 'We would see a sign!' The word within a word, unable to speak a word, Swaddled with darkness. In the juvescence of the year Came Christ the tiger In depraved May, dogwood and chestnut, flowering judas, To be eaten, to be divided, to be drunk Among whispers; by Mr. Silvero With caressing hands, at Limoges Who walked all night in the next room; By Hakagawa, bowing among the Titians; By Madame de Tornquist, in the dark room Shifting the candles; Fraulein von Kulp Who turned in the hall, one hand on the door. Vacant shuttles Weave the wind. I have no ghosts, An old man in a draughty house Under a windy knob. After such knowledge, what forgiveness? Think now History has many cunning passages, contrived corridors And issues, deceives with whispering ambitions, Guides us by vanities. Think now She gives when our attention is distracted And what she gives, gives with such supple confusions That the giving famishes the craving. Gives too late What's not believed in, or is still believed, In memory only, reconsidered passion. Gives too soon Into weak hands, what's thought can be dispensed with Till the refusal propagates a fear. Think Neither fear nor courage saves us. Unnatural vices Are fathered by our heroism. Virtues Are forced upon us by our impudent crimes. These tears are shaken from the wrath-bearing tree. The tiger springs in the new year. Us he devours. Think at last We have not reached conclusion, when I Stiffen in a rented house. Think at last I have not made this show purposelessly And it is not by any concitation Of the backward devils. I would meet you upon this honestly. I that was near your heart was removed therefrom To lose beauty in terror, terror in inquisition. I have lost my passion: why should I need to keep it Since what is kept must be adulterated? I have lost my sight, smell, hearing, taste and touch: How should I use it for your closer contact? These with a thousand small deliberations Protract the profit of their chilled delirium, Excite the membrane, when the sense has cooled, With pungent sauces, multiply variety In a wilderness of mirrors. What will the spider do Suspend its operations, will the weevil Delay? De Bailhache, Fresca, Mrs. Cammel, whirled Beyond the circuit of the shuddering Bear In fractured atoms. Gull against the wind, in the windy straits Of Belle Isle, or running on the Horn, White feathers in the snow, the Gulf claims, And an old man driven by the Trades To a sleepy corner. Tenants of the house, Thoughts of a dry brain in a dry season.

name_of_work: Listening to Michael Jackson in Tehran by Ali Alizadeh
content: Smuggled across the fierce chasm between us and the US, and then hidden, stuffed between Farsi and Science textbooks in my school bag, the illegal and sacrilegious cassette-tape of Thriller, ready for revelation to the sheepish, ignorant kids on the bus to my primary school in war-stricken Tehran. My plan: to expose the forbidden thing, exhibit my courage, rebelliousness, etc. Autumn of '83, desperate for attention/approval from the other kids. My copy of dangerous Western 'art' would unsettle the boring, Islamic world of my classmates - and elevate my cowardly, chubby, unpopular self. I whispered to the kid next to me if he had ever heard of 'Billie Jean' and 'Beat It'; if he knew anything at all about the number one famous star of our wicked enemy. "I love Thriller! Aren't the zombies so scary in the music video! They're so ugly!" His boisterous words echoed. The bus vibrated with the singer's name. Another shouted he had a Thriller poster, and another, a 'Billie Jean' T-shirt, a gift from Turkey. Silenced, robbed of my planned stardom, I sank in my seat; later threw out my Thriller tape, the fetish of Great Satan's useless, ubiquitous popular culture.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very patient when he waited for his mommy to come back with carrots. One day, Benny heard a loud noise and got scared. He wanted to escape, but he didn't know where to go. He decided to hide under a bush until the noise went away. After a while, Benny peeked out from under the bush and saw that it was just a bird singing. Benny felt silly for being scared and went back to patiently waiting for his mommy to come back with carrots.

Granted, we die for good. Life, then, is largely a thing Of happens to like, not should. And that, too, granted, why Do I happen to like red bush, Grey grass and green-gray sky? What else remains? But red, Gray, green, why those of all? That is not what I said: Not those of all. But those. One likes what one happens to like. One likes the way red grows. It cannot matter at all. Happens to like is one Of the ways things happen to fall.

Once upon a day, there was a curious girl. Her name was Lucy. She wanted to explore the world and find out what was out there. 
Suddenly she heard a noise. She went to investigate the sound. It was coming from the garden. 
She saw a rabbit. He was hopping around and did not seem scared. 
Lucy asked, "What are you doing?" 
The rabbit said, "Let me show you. Follow me!" 
So Lucy followed the rabbit. He took her around the garden, showing her all the different things that he liked. 
When they were finished, the rabbit said, "Now do you know why I was so curious about this place?" 
Lucy smiled and said, "Yes, I do!" 
The rabbit ran back into the bushes, leaving Lucy to explore the garden by herself. She was happy and felt content. 
And that is how Lucy spent her curious day!

Once upon a time, there lived an elderly man. He was a very kind man and he liked to teach people things. One day, he decided to teach a young boy about apples. 

The elderly man took the boy to an apple tree. He taught the boy how to pick the apples and how to tell a ripe one from an unripe one. He showed him how to put the apples in a basket. 

When it was time to go home, the elderly man took the apples back with him. He taught the boy how to make an apple pie. They peeled the apples, chopped them up and put them in a pie dish with some cinnamon, sugar and butter. 

When the pie was finished they both enjoyed a sweet and juicy slice and the boy thanked the elderly man for teaching him all about apples.

name_of_work: Our Deepest Fear by Marianne Williamson
content: Our deepest fear is not that we are inadequate. Our deepest fear is that we are powerful beyond measure. It is our light, not our darkness that most frightens us. We ask ourselves, "Who am I to be brilliant, gorgeous, talented, fabulous?" Actually, who are you not to be? You are a child of God. Your playing small does not serve the world. There's nothing enlightened about shrinking so that other people won't feel insecure around you. We are all meant to shine, as children do. We were born to make manifest the glory of God that is within us. It's not just in some of us; it's in everyone. And as we let our own light shine, we unconsciously give other people permission to do the same. As we're liberated from our own fear, our presence automatically liberates others.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved her pretty skirt that twirled around when she spun. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a butterfly. She was so excited and started to run after it. 

Suddenly, the wind blew and her skirt flew up! Lily was embarrassed and wanted to shut her eyes. But her mom said it was okay and helped her fix her skirt. Lily felt better and continued to chase the butterfly. 

When it was time to go home, Lily was sad to leave the park but happy to have had a fun day. She went to bed that night dreaming of twirling in her skirt and chasing butterflies again.

name_of_work: Oh Who is that Young Sinner by A. E. Houseman
content: Oh who is that young sinner with the handcuffs on his wrists? And what has he been after that they groan and shake their fists? And wherefore is he wearing such a conscience-stricken air? Oh they're taking him to prison for the colour of his hair. 'Tis a shame to human nature, such a head of hair as his; In the good old time 'twas hanging for the colour that it is; Though hanging isn't bad enough and flaying would be fair For the nameless and abominable colour of his hair. Oh a deal of pains he's taken and a pretty price he's paid To hide his poll or dye it of a mentionable shade; But they've pulled the beggar's hat off for the world to see and stare, And they're haling him to justice for the colour of his hair. Now 'tis oakum for his fingers and the treadmill for his feet And the quarry-gang on Portland in the cold and in the heat, And between his spells of labour in the time he has to spare He can curse the God that made him for the colour of his hair.

One day, a little girl named Amy found an unknown box in her room. She did not know what was inside. She had a question in her mind. She asked her mom, "What is in this box?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Open it and see!" Amy opened the box and found a big, yummy waffle. She was so happy. She shared the waffle with her mom.

They both sat down and ate the waffle together. It was the best waffle they ever had. From that day on, Amy always looked for unknown boxes with a question in her mind, hoping to find more yummy treats.

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk. She wore her unusual coat with many colors. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing.

As she walked, she met a small cat. The cat said, "Meow, Lily, you should warn your mom that it might rain later." Lily looked at the sky, but it was still blue and sunny. "Thank you, cat," she said, "I will tell her."

Lily ran back home and told her mom about the cat's warning. Her mom smiled and said, "That's very kind of the cat, but I think we will be okay." They both looked outside, and the sun was still shining. Lily felt happy that she had helped, and she went back to play outside with her unusual coat.
