From lowered blinds the dark folk stare, And here the fair folk talk, Indignant that these two should dare In unison to walk. Oblivious to look and word They pass, and see no wonder That lightning brilliant as a sword Should blaze the path of thunder.

name_of_work: Before The Cask of Wine by Li Bai
content: The spring wind comes from the east and quickly passes, Leaving faint ripples in the wine of the golden bowl. The flowers fall, flake after flake, myriads together. You, pretty girl, wine-flushed, Your rosy face is rosier still. How long may the peach and plum trees flower By the green-painted house? The fleeting light deceives man, Brings soon the stumbling age. Rise and dance In the westering sun While the urge of youthful years is yet unsubdued! What avails to lament after one's hair has turned white like silken threads?

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She had a big, red ball. One day, Lucy and her friend, Tom, played with the ball in the park. They had to be careful not to let the ball roll away.

Lucy and Tom had fun playing with the ball. They would throw it and then run to catch it. They laughed and played all day. But then, it was time for Lucy to go home. Lucy and Tom had to part and say goodbye.

As they said goodbye, Tom's mom gave Lucy a reward for being a good friend. She gave Lucy a big, shiny sticker. Lucy was so happy and said thank you. She couldn't wait to play with Tom again.

name_of_work: 'The Trial by Existence' by Robert Frost
content: Even the bravest that are slain Shall not dissemble their surprise On waking to find valor reign, Even as on earth, in paradise; And where they sought without the sword Wide field of asphodel fore'er, To find that the utmost reward Of daring should be still to dare. The light of heaven falls whole and white And is not shattered into dyes, The light for ever is morning light; The hills are verdured pasture-wise; The angel hosts with freshness go, And seek with laughter what to brave;-- And binding all is the hushed snow Of the far-distant breaking wave. And from a cliff-top is proclaimed The gathering of the souls for birth, The trial by existence named, The obscuration upon earth. And the slant spirits trooping by In streams and cross- and counter-streams Can but give ear to that sweet cry For its suggestion of what dreams! And the more loitering are turned To view once more the sacrifice Of those who for some good discerned Will gladly give up paradise. And a white shimmering concourse rolls Toward the throne to witness there The speeding of devoted souls Which God makes his especial care. And none are taken but who will, Having first heard the life read out That opens earthward, good and ill, Beyond the shadow of a doubt; And very beautifully God limns, And tenderly, life's little dream, But naught extenuates or dims, Setting the thing that is supreme. Nor is there wanting in the press Some spirit to stand simply forth, Heroic in its nakedness, Against the uttermost of earth. The tale of earth's unhonored things Sounds nobler there than 'neath the sun; And the mind whirls and the heart sings, And a shout greets the daring one. But always God speaks at the end: 'One thought in agony of strife The bravest would have by for friend, The memory that he chose the life; But the pure fate to which you go Admits no memory of choice, Or the woe were not earthly woe To which you give the assenting voice.' And so the choice must be again, But the last choice is still the same; And the awe passes wonder then, And a hush falls for all acclaim. And God has taken a flower of gold And broken it, and used therefrom The mystic link to bind and hold Spirit to matter till death come. 'Tis of the essence of life here, Though we choose greatly, still to lack The lasting memory at all clear, That life has for us on the wrack Nothing but what we somehow chose; Thus are we wholly stripped of pride In the pain that has but one close, Bearing it crushed and mystified.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain. On the mountain, there lived a little boy named Tim and a little girl named Sue. They were friends and liked to play together.

One day, while they were playing, Tim pinched Sue's arm. Sue said, "Ouch! That hurt!" Tim said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it would hurt you." Sue said, "It's okay, but please don't do it again." Tim was ignorant about pinching, but now he knew better.

From that day on, Tim and Sue played on the mountain without any pinching. They had lots of fun together and learned many new things. And they lived happily ever after.

I have gone out, a possessed witch, haunting the black air, braver at night; dreaming evil, I have done my hitch over the plain houses, light by light: lonely thing, twelve-fingered, out of mind. A woman like that is not a woman, quite. I have been her kind. I have found the warm caves in the woods, filled them with skillets, carvings, shelves, closets, silks, innumerable goods; fixed the suppers for the worms and the elves: whining, rearranging the disaligned. A woman like that is misunderstood. I have been her kind. I have ridden in your cart, driver, waved my nude arms at villages going by, learning the last bright routes, survivor where your flames still bite my thigh and my ribs crack where your wheels wind. A woman like that is not ashamed to die. I have been her kind.

Once upon a time there was a healthy girl who had a special bow. She wanted to reach high in the sky with her bow so she stood at the edge of a hill. The girl stretched her arms up with the bow in her hands. She twirled and spun, stretching her arms even higher. All of a sudden, she felt herself reach the clouds. She was so happy. She spun around and around until she touched the stars in the sky. Then she came back down to the hill, feeling very proud of herself for reaching so high. She hugged her bow tightly, happy that she had done something special. She smiled, knowing she had reached something amazing.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie was very graceful and loved to fly in the sky. One day, Tweetie saw some seeds on the ground and wanted to gather them for her family. But, as she was gathering the seeds, she saw a big cat coming towards her. 

"Hey, Tweetie, what are you doing?" asked the cat.

"I'm gathering seeds for my family," replied Tweetie.

"Well, those seeds are mine. Give them to me," said the cat, trying to take the seeds away.

"No, they are mine. I gathered them fair and square," said Tweetie, flapping her wings.

The cat tried to grab the seeds again, but he accidentally tripped and fell. Tweetie quickly flew away with the seeds and brought them back to her family. They were very happy and grateful for the delicious seeds. From that day on, Tweetie knew that even though she was small, she could still be brave and stand up for herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a soft pink velvet pillow that she loved to hug. One day, her friend Tommy came over and didn't have a pillow to rest his head on. Lily wanted to help him, so she decided to lend him her comfortable velvet pillow. Tommy was very happy and thanked Lily for being so kind. He fell asleep right away and had the best nap ever. When he woke up, he gave the pillow back to Lily and said it was the most comfortable thing he ever felt. From that day on, Lily and Tommy were the best of friends and shared everything, including their favorite velvet things.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to imagine they were explorers in a jungle. They had a big stick for a sword and a hat for a helmet.

"Look, Tom, a spike!" Lily said, pointing to a rose bush. "Maybe it is a dragon's tail. We have to be careful."

Tom nodded. He wanted to be brave. He held his stick and approached the bush. He pretended to fight the dragon. He swung his stick and hit the spike.

"Ow!" Tom cried. He dropped his stick and held his hand. He saw blood on his finger. He felt pain and fear.

Lily ran to him. She saw his wound. She felt sorry and scared. She hugged him and said, "Don't cry, Tom. It's okay. You are not careless. You are a hero. Let's go to mom. She will make it better."

Once there was a big, hot summer and it made everyone very miserable. Everyone wanted to relax, but it was too hot.

One day, a little girl asked her dad if he could help her be comfortable again. So her dad made her a little pool with water in it. They both put their feet in the pool and it felt so nice.

They both stayed in the pool all day and it was so much fun. Soon, the little girl and her dad were feeling much better and relaxed.

The summer was still miserable, but at least the little girl and her dad had their pool to help them relax.

Evening will come, however determined the late afternoon, Limes and oaks in their last green flush, pearled in September mist. I have conjured a lily to light these hours, a token of thanks, Zones and auras of soft glare framing the brilliant globes. A promise made and kept for life - that was your gift - Because of which, here is a gift in return, glovewort to some, Each shining bonnet guarded by stern lance-like leaves. The country loaded its whole self into your slender hands, Hands that can rest, now, relieved of a century's weight. Evening has come. Rain on the black lochs and dark Munros. Lily of the Valley, a namesake almost, a favourite flower Interlaced with your famous bouquets, the restrained Zeal and forceful grace of its lanterns, each inflorescence A silent bell disguising a singular voice. A blurred new day Breaks uncrowned on remote peaks and public parks, and Everything turns on these luminous petals and deep roots, This lily that thrives between spire and tree, whose brightness Holds and glows beyond the life and border of its bloom.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. They have bikes with pedals. They can ride fast and have fun.

One day, Tim and Mia go to the park. They see a big hill. Tim says, "Let's go up the hill. It will be fun." Mia says, "OK, let's go."

They step on their pedals and start to go up the hill. It is hard. They have to push hard. They get tired. Mia says, "I want to stop. It is too hard." Tim says, "No, don't stop. We can do it. Come on."

They keep going. They reach the top of the hill. They are happy. They see a lot of things. They see trees and flowers and birds and clouds. They see the pond and the swings and the slide. They see other kids playing.

Tim says, "Wow, look at all the things we can see. It is beautiful." Mia says, "Yes, it is. I'm glad we came up here. It was worth it." Tim says, "Me too. I'm glad you are my friend. You are brave and strong." Mia says, "Thank you. You are my friend too. You are kind and helpful."

They smile at each other. They step on their pedals and start to go down the hill. They go fast and have fun. They laugh and shout. They are happy. They are friends.

I love all films that start with rain: rain, braiding a windowpane or darkening a hung-out dress or streaming down her upturned face; one big thundering downpour right through the empty script and score before the act, before the blame, before the lens pulls through the frame to where the woman sits alone beside a silent telephone or the dress lies ruined on the grass or the girl walks off the overpass, and all things flow out from that source along their fatal watercourse. However bad or overlong such a film can do no wrong, so when his native twang shows through or when the boom dips into view or when her speech starts to betray its adaptation from the play, I think to when we opened cold on a starlit gutter, running gold with the neon drugstore sign and I'd read into its blazing line: forget the ink, the milk, the blood-- all was washed clean with the flood we rose up from the falling waters the fallen rain's own sons and daughters and none of this, none of this matters.

Lily liked to eat yogurt every morning. She had a special bowl and spoon for her yogurt. She kept them in a drawer in the kitchen. She was very organized.

One day, she woke up and went to the kitchen. She opened the drawer and took out her bowl and spoon. She looked for the yogurt in the fridge. But she could not find it. She saw milk, cheese, eggs, and juice. But no yogurt.

She felt sad and confused. Where was her yogurt? She asked her mom, who was making toast. "Mom, where is my yogurt?" she said.

Her mom smiled and pointed to a new place. "Your yogurt is in the pantry, Lily. I bought a big box of yogurt cups. You can pull one out and peel the lid. It is easier and less messy than the big tub of yogurt."

Lily looked at the pantry. She saw a big box with pictures of yogurt cups. She walked over and pulled one out. It was pink and had strawberries on it. She liked strawberries. She peeled the lid and saw the creamy yogurt inside. She dipped her spoon and tasted it. It was yummy.

She smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I like the new yogurt. It is easy and tasty. And I can still use my bowl and spoon."

Her mom hugged her and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like it. You are a very organized and smart girl."

Once there was a cricket. He was fair and very playful. He loved to kick and play. Every day he would look for something to kick. One day he found a ball and was so excited. He picked it up and from the top of a hill he kicked the ball. It rolled and rolled until it stopped at the bottom. The cricket raced down the hill so that he could kick it again. He had so much fun kicking the ball up and down the hill. He kicked it until it was time to go home. The cricket was very happy, he had a fair day of fun playing with his new ball.

Once upon a time there was a brave police. He liked to learn new things. He studied every day so he could help people in the village.

One day, he decided to visit a big city. He had never been there before. He went to explore but he did not remember the way home. He was lost and could not find his way back.

He tried to ask people for help but nobody would help him. Nobody wanted to talk to the police. They were too scared.

The brave police never returned home. He was lost in the big city forever. Nobody ever learned of his brave deeds. The police was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy found a long rope lying on the ground. He picked it up and started to play with it.

Suddenly, Timmy's friend Billy came over and asked, "What are you doing, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "I found this rope and I'm playing with it. Do you want to play too?" Billy was glad to join in.

Together, they played with the rope and had so much fun. After a while, they decided it was time to settle down and rest. They sat on the grass and talked about all the things they saw and did that day. Timmy was glad to have such a good friend like Billy.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in the forest. He liked to go on adventures and explore new places. One day, he met a little bird who wanted to go on an adventure too. The bear said, "Let's go on an adventure together!" and the bird said, "Yes, let's go!"

They walked and walked for many days and many nights. They saw lots of trees and flowers and animals. The bear and the bird talked and talked about all the things they saw. They talked about the big year they had ahead of them and all the fun they were going to have.

Finally, they came to a big mountain. The bear said, "Let's climb to the top!" The bird said, "That sounds adventurous!" So they climbed and climbed until they reached the top. They looked out over the whole forest and saw how beautiful it was. They were happy they went on an adventure together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she found a big box. She wanted to know what was inside, so she opened it. 

Inside the box, there was a balloon. She blew it up and held it tight. Suddenly, the balloon popped and she couldn't breathe. She needed oxygen! 

Luckily, her mommy was nearby and she quickly revealed a small bottle of oxygen. She put the mask on Lily's face and she could breathe again. From that day on, Lily knew to be careful with balloons and always ask for help when she needs it.

name_of_work: The Country of the Blind by C.S. Lewis
content: Hard light bathed them-a whole nation of eyeless men, Dark bipeds not aware how they were maimed. A long Process, clearly, a slow curse, Drained through centuries, left them thus. At some transitional stage, then, a luckless few, No doubt, must have had eyes after the up-to-date, Normal type had achieved snug Darkness, safe from the guns of heavn; Whose blind mouths would abuse words that belonged to their Great-grandsires, unabashed, talking of light in some Eunuch'd, etiolated, Fungoid sense, as a symbol of Abstract thoughts. If a man, one that had eyes, a poor Misfit, spoke of the grey dawn or the stars or green- Sloped sea waves, or admired how Warm tints change in a lady's cheek, None complained he had used words from an alien tongue, None question'd. It was worse. All would agree 'Of course,' Came their answer. "We've all felt Just like that." They were wrong. And he Knew too much to be clear, could not explain. The words -- Sold, raped flung to the dogs -- now could avail no more; Hence silence. But the mouldwarps, With glib confidence, easily Showed how tricks of the phrase, sheer metaphors could set Fools concocting a myth, taking the worlds for things. Do you think this a far-fetched Picture? Go then about among Men now famous; attempt speech on the truths that once, Opaque, carved in divine forms, irremovable, Dear but dear as a mountain- Mass, stood plain to the inward eye.

One morning, there was a big boy who was feeling sad. He started to cry. His mom asked him what was wrong, but the boy just kept crying. She gave him a big hug and said, "Let's get you some cereal. That will make you feel better." 

The boy still looked sad, so his mom said, "Just try it. It's really yummy." The boy slowly walked to the kitchen and sat down at the table. He was still sniffling a bit, but he picked up the spoon and started to eat the cereal. 

And then, something happened. As the boy ate more and more of the cereal, he started to smile. Soon, there were big smiles on his face and he was laughing. He said to his mom, "This cereal is really yummy! Thank you for making me feel better.â€ 

The mom smiled and said, "Anytime. You can always count on me and cereal."

name_of_work: The Truth the Dead Know by Anne Sexton
content: Gone, I say and walk from church, refusing the stiff procession to the grave, letting the dead ride alone in the hearse. It is June. I am tired of being brave. We drive to the Cape. I cultivate myself where the sun gutters from the sky, where the sea swings in like an iron gate and we touch. In another country people die. My darling, the wind falls in like stones from the whitehearted water and when we touch we enter touch entirely. No one's alone. Men kill for this, or for as much. And what of the dead? They lie without shoes in their stone boats. They are more like stone than the sea would be if it stopped. They refuse to be blessed, throat, eye and knucklebone.

Once upon a time there were two friends; Ben and Jill.

Ben liked to count numbers. He would number stars and clouds, and trees and leaves. Ben liked to be busy counting the things around him.

One day Jill had an idea. She said to Ben, â€œLetâ€™s go outside and count some wild things!â€ Ben and Jill went outside and saw lots of wild animals. They counted butterflies and birds, and cats and dogs.

But then it started to get cold, and Ben and Jill had to go inside. They counted all the items that were inside - chairs and tables, books and toys - but it wasnâ€™t as much fun as counting wild things outside!

Once upon a time there was a small bunny. He had two soft ears and a little white nose. His name was Timmy.

One day, Timmy was hopping in the garden when he saw something that looked tasty. It was a small, juicy carrot! He hopped over to it, and started chewing. He chewed and chewed and it was delicious!

He hopped away to find some more carrots, but instead he found a tasty, green leaf. He started chewing it too and it was just as good.

He kept hopping and looking for something yummy to chew. He found some juicy apples and chewy berries, so he munched away.

Finally, he was full! He dug a little burrow and curled up in it and took a nap.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little bear named Brown. He was very lonely, as all of the other bears were afraid of him because his fur was a strange gray color.

One day, Brown saw a tree with a lot of leaves in a field nearby. He decided to go and investigate. When he arrived he saw that some of the leaves had been cut into pieces. Brown didn't know why, it was very strange. He began to look more carefully and saw that the leaves were all filthy - covered in dirt and bits of twig. 

Brown was really angry. Who had done this? He looked around and saw that there was no one there.

Brown didn't want any other trees in the forest to get damaged like this, so he decided that he would patrol the field every day to make sure nothing like this happened again.

This story teaches us that it is important to look out for our environment, and to make sure we take care of it. Even if it looks like no one else is caring for the environment, it is still our responsibility to do the right thing.

name_of_work: On the Beach at Fontana by James Joyce
content: Wind whines and whines the shingle, The crazy pierstakes groan; A senile sea numbers each single Slimesilvered stone. From whining wind and colder Grey sea I wrap him warm And touch his trembling fineboned shoulder And boyish arm. Around us fear, descending Darkness of fear above And in my heart how deep unending Ache of love!

name_of_work: If You Forget Me by Pablo Neruda
content: I want you to know one thing. You know how this is: if I look at the crystal moon, at the red branch of the slow autumn at my window, if I touch near the fire the impalpable ash or the wrinkled body of the log, everything carries me to you, as if everything that exists, aromas, light, metals, were little boats that sail toward those isles of yours that wait for me. Well, now, if little by little you stop loving me I shall stop loving you little by little. If suddenly you forget me do not look for me, for I shall already have forgotten you. If you think it long and mad, the wind of banners that passes through my life, and you decide to leave me at the shore of the heart where I have roots, remember that on that day, at that hour, I shall lift my arms and my roots will set off to seek another land. But if each day, each hour, you feel that you are destined for me with implacable sweetness, if each day a flower climbs up to your lips to seek me, ah my love, ah my own, in me all that fire is repeated, in me nothing is extinguished or forgotten, my love feeds on your love, beloved, and as long as you live it will be in your arms without leaving mine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to fly. She told her mom about it and her mom decided to explain the science behind why she couldn't fly. She took her daughter to the doctor's office to show her an x-ray. 

"See this?" Mom said as she pointed at the x-ray. "Humans can't fly because of all of these bones. We can't make our wings like a bird can."

The little girl's face lit up. "You mean if I had wings like a bird then I could fly?"

Mom smiled. "Yes. But it's very difficult to do. We just have to be happy that birds can fly and people can't."

The little girl thought about it for a few moments. Then she smiled and said, "It's ok. I'm happy that birds can fly. That makes me feel better!"

Mom hugged her daughter and said, "That's a great attitude to have! Remember, it's ok if things are difficult. We just have to keep trying and stay positive."

The little girl nodded and went back to playing, content with her newfound knowledge. 

The moral of the story is that it's ok for things to be difficult, but it's important to stay positive and keep trying.

1 I cradled my newborn daughter and felt the heartbeat pull me out of shock. She didn't know what her hands were: she folded them. I asked her was there a place where there was no world. She didn't know what a voice was: her lips were the shape of a nipple. 2 In the park the child says: watch me. It will not count unless you see. And she shows me the cartwheel, the skip, the tumble, the tricks performed at leisure in midair, each unknown until it is finished. At home she orders: see me eat. I watch her curl on herself, sleep; as I try to leave the dark room her dreaming voice commands me: watch. 3 Always we passed the seesaw on the way to the swings but tonight I remember the principle of the lever, I sit the child at one end, I sit near the center, the fulcrum, at once she has power to lift me off the earth and keep me suspended by her tiny weight, she laughing, I stunned at the power of the formula.

Once upon a time, there was a big round ball. But the ball was not happy. He wanted to lie down and stay still. So he rolled away, looking for a pleasant place he could lie in.

Finally, he found the perfect spot. He rolled and lay down in the grass. He was glad and smiled to himself.

Suddenly, a big hand came down. It grabbed the ball and threw it away. The ball was so scared. He lay there in the distance, far away from his dream spot.

The ball was so sad but he could not move. He stayed there, all alone, until the end of the day. And he never found his dream spot again.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the park. She saw a silly dog playing with an orange ball. The dog was jumping and running around. Amy thought it was funny and wanted to play too.

Amy asked the dog, "Can I play with you?" The dog wagged its tail and barked. They played together, throwing the orange ball and laughing. The dog was very good at catching the ball in its mouth.

Soon, it was time for Amy to go home. She said goodbye to the dog and walked away. As she left, she didn't recognize that she had dropped her toy. The next day, she went back to the park and saw the silly dog again. The dog had her toy in its mouth and was waiting for her. Amy was so happy to see her toy and thanked the dog. They played together again, and from that day on, they became best friends.

Once upon a time there was a big barber. He loved to cut peoples' hair. One day he had a strange feeling. He began to shrink until he was very small. He couldn't believe it.

He started to look for help and he found a big dog. "Please help me," said the barber. The big dog understood and he licked the barber. Suddenly, the barber started to get bigger and bigger again.

The barber was so happy and he thanked the big dog. Then he went back to his barber shop and started cutting peoples' hair. He was glad that he was not small anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the mud. One day, Lily was playing in the mud when her friend Max came over.

"Hi Lily, what are you doing?" Max asked.

"I'm playing in the mud. Do you want to play with me?" Lily asked.

Max thought about it for a moment and said, "I don't want to get my clothes dirty."

"It's okay, Max. We can wash them later. Let's unite and have fun together!" Lily said.

Max decided to join Lily and they both played in the mud together. They made mud pies and splashed in the mud puddles. When they were finished, they both had to take a fine shower to clean themselves up. They had so much fun playing together in the mud that they couldn't wait to do it again.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big car on the road. The car is shiny and has four doors. It looks very rich.

"Wow, look at that car!" Ben says. "It is so big and nice. I wish I had a car like that."

Anna looks at the car too. She does not think it is nice. She thinks it is loud and dirty. She likes her bike better. It is small and quiet. She can ride it fast and have fun.

"I don't like that car," Anna says. "It makes too much noise and smoke. It hurts the air and the trees. I like my bike more. It is good for me and the park."

Ben and Anna have different ideas. They talk to each other. They try to understand why they like different things. They are still friends. They agree to play with both the car and the bike. They share and take turns. They have fun in the park.

Once there was a mighty goose that liked to write. He wrote stories, songs and letters. Everywhere he went, he wrote something. He wrote in the fields, he wrote in the mountains, he wrote in the forests. 

One day, he decided to write a letter in the pond. But when he dropped his paper into the water, a big wave came and it washed it away. 

The mighty goose was very sad - he had lost his letter. He realised though, that it was his own fault - if he had written it in the ground or on a rock, it would not have been lost. 

The moral of the story was that sometimes it's important to choose the right place for things, otherwise it may get lost!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a pretty skirt that she liked to wear all the time. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends.

At the park, Sue saw a big rock and decided to sit on it. But when she sat down, she heard a rip sound. Sue looked down and saw that her skirt had a big hole in it. She felt sad and thought it was stupid that her skirt ripped so easily.

Sue went home and showed her mom the hole in her skirt. Her mom gave her a hug and said, "Don't worry, we can fix it." They sewed the skirt together and Sue was happy that she could wear her pretty skirt again. From that day on, Sue was more careful when she sat down, and she never felt stupid again.

Sara was very happy. Today was her birthday and she was having a party. She invited her friends from school and they came with gifts and balloons. Sara's mom made a big cake with candles and sprinkles. Sara's dad played music and games.

"Let's play pin the tail on the donkey!" Sara's dad said. He gave each child a paper tail with tape and a blindfold. He spun them around and pointed them to the wall where a picture of a donkey was. The children tried to stick the tail on the right spot, but they missed and made funny shapes. Sara and her friends laughed and laughed. They thought it was very fun.

Then it was time to open the gifts. Sara sat on the floor and her friends gave her their presents. She opened them one by one and said thank you. She got a doll, a book, a puzzle, a hat, and a teddy bear. She liked them all, but her favorite was the teddy bear. It was brown and soft and had a red bow. Sara hugged it and said, "You are so cute! I love you, teddy!"

Sara's mom brought the cake and everyone sang happy birthday. Sara blew out the candles and made a wish. She wished for more fun and laughter with her friends and family. She cut the cake and shared it with everyone. It was yummy and sweet. Sara and her friends ate and talked and smiled. They had a great time at the party. Sara was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Teddy. Teddy was very pretty with soft brown fur and big, round eyes. One day, Teddy met a little girl named Lily. Lily had an opinion that Teddy was the best bear ever. She hugged Teddy tightly and didn't want to let go.

Teddy was very happy to have a friend like Lily. They played together every day and had lots of fun. But one day, Lily had to move away to a faraway place. Teddy was sad and missed her very much. He wished she could come back and hug him again.

Days turned into weeks and weeks turned into months. Teddy waited and waited, but Lily never came back. He became very lonely and sad. One day, Teddy couldn't take it anymore and decided to go look for Lily.

He walked and walked until he was very tired. Finally, he found a big city with lots of people. But he couldn't find Lily anywhere. Teddy was lost and didn't know what to do. He missed Lily so much that he started to cry. Sadly, Teddy never found his friend Lily and he was alone forever.

One day, a creative figure drove to the park. He said to himself, "I can't wait to explore this park and have some fun!"

He spread out a big blanket, and out of his pocket, he took out his toy car. He got on his knees and drove it around the blanket. He was having so much fun!

Just then he heard someone say, "Hey buddy, that looks like so much fun!".

He looked up and saw a little girl who was about three years old. She was clapping her hands and grinning from ear to ear.

The figure smiled and said, "Do you want to come and drive with me?"
The little girl's face lit up and she quickly grabbed the car and started driving it around.

They both laughed and had a great time as they drove around the park. It was the best day ever!

Sara and Ben wanted to make a snowman. They put on their warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They went outside and saw a lot of snow on the ground. They were happy.

They rolled a big ball of snow for the body. They rolled a smaller ball of snow for the head. They put the head on top of the body. They found two sticks for the arms, a carrot for the nose, and some stones for the eyes and mouth. They gave their snowman a smile.

But then, a strong wind blew. The snowman's head fell off. Sara and Ben were frustrated. They tried to put the head back on, but it was too heavy. They needed support.

They saw their dad coming from the house. He had a shovel in his hand. He saw their snowman and their sad faces. He asked them what was wrong.

"Our snowman's head fell off. We can't put it back on. It's too heavy. We need support," Sara and Ben said.

"Don't worry, I can help you," their dad said. He used the shovel to make a pile of snow behind the snowman's body. He lifted the head and placed it on the pile. He pressed the snow around the head to make it stable. He gave their snowman a scarf.

"There, now your snowman has support. He won't fall off again," their dad said.

Sara and Ben thanked their dad. They hugged their snowman. They were happy.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to school. He loved to draw with chalk on the big, wide blackboard. One day, Timmy's teacher told him to write his name on a piece of paper and mail it to his friend. Timmy was excited to do this because he loved getting mail. He wrote his name very carefully and put it in an envelope. Then he walked to the mailbox and put the envelope inside. Timmy waited and waited for his friend's letter to come back in the mail. Finally, it arrived and Timmy was so happy. He showed his friend the wide chalk drawings he had made at school. They both laughed and had fun together. The end.

If you can keep your money when governments about you Are losing theirs and blaming it on you, If you can trust your neighbour when they trust not you And they be very nosy too; If you can await the warm delights of summer Then summer comes and goes with sun not seen, And pay so much for drinking water Knowing that the water is unclean. If you seek peace in times of war creation, And you can see that oil merchants are to blame, If you can meet a pimp or politician, And treat those two impostors just the same; If you cannot bear dis-united nations And you think this new world order is a trick, If you've ever tried to build good race relations, And watch bad policing mess your work up quick. If you can make one heap of all your savings And risk buying a small house and plot, Then sit back and watch the economy inflating Then have to deal with the negative equity you've got; If you can force your mind and body to continue When all the social services have gone, If you struggle on when there is nothing in you, Except the knowledge that justice can be wrong. If you can speak the truth to common people Or walk with Kings and Queens and live no lie, If you can see how power can be evil And know that every censor is a spy; If you can fill an unforgiving lifetime With years of working hard to make ends meet, You may not be wealthy but I am sure you will find That you can hold your head high as you walk the streets.

name_of_work: The Way Through the Woods by Rudyard Kipling
content: They shut the road through the woods Seventy years ago. Weather and rain have undone it again, And now you would never know There was once a road through the woods Before they planted the trees. It is underneath the coppice and heath, And the thin anemones. Only the keeper sees That, where the ring-dove broods, And the badgers roll at ease, There was once a road through the woods. Yet, if you enter the woods Of a summer evening late, When the night-air cools on the trout-ringed pools Where the otter whistles his mate, (They fear not men in the woods, Because they see so few.) You will hear the beat of a horse's feet, And the swish of a skirt in the dew, Steadily cantering through The misty solitudes, As though they perfectly knew The old lost road through the woods. But there is no road through the woods.

Once upon a time there was a grandma and a grandpa who lived in a big house. Grandma and Grandpa loved making music, so they always played instruments together.

One day, they decided to record a song. Grandpa opened the door to the room where they kept all the music instruments. He was so excited!

Grandma took out her guitar and started strumming. Grandpa grabbed a drum and began to beat. They made a really wonderful song! Grandpa picked up the microphone to record it.

Grandpa and Grandma were obedient and followed all the instructions for recording the song. After a few tries, they had a perfect song recorded!

They were so proud and happy with their song. They listened to it over and over again and danced around the room. It was the best day ever!

I love you as a sheriff searches for a walnut That will solve a murder case unsolved for years Because the murderer left it in the snow beside a window Through which he saw her head, connecting with Her shoulders by a neck, and laid a red Roof in her heart. For this we live a thousand years; For this we love, and we live because we love, we are not Inside a bottle, thank goodness! I love you as a Kid searches for a goat; I am crazier than shirttails In the wind, when you're near, a wind that blows from The big blue sea, so shiny so deep and so unlike us; I think I am bicycling across an Africa of green and white fields Always, to be near you, even in my heart When I'm awake, which swims, and also I believe that you Are trustworthy as the sidewalk which leads me to The place where I again think of you, a new Harmony of thoughts! I love you as the sunlight leads the prow Of a ship which sails From Hartford to Miami, and I love you Best at dawn, when even before I am awake the sun Receives me in the questions which you always pose.

name_of_work: Life is Fine by Langston Hughes
content: I went down to the river, I set down on the bank. I tried to think but couldn't, So I jumped in and sank. I came up once and hollered! I came up twice and cried! If that water hadn't a-been so cold I might've sunk and died. But it was Cold in that water! It was cold! I took the elevator Sixteen floors above the ground. I thought about my baby And thought I would jump down. I stood there and I hollered! I stood there and I cried! If it hadn't a-been so high I might've jumped and died. But it was High up there! It was high! So since I'm still here livin', I guess I will live on. I could've died for love-- But for livin' I was born Though you may hear me holler, And you may see me cry-- I'll be dogged, sweet baby, If you gonna see me die. Life is fine! Fine as wine! Life is fine!

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a hidden motorcycle in the bushes near their house. It was big and shiny and had two wheels.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "Can we ride it?"

"I don't know," Lily said. "It's not ours. Maybe someone is looking for it."

Tom did not care. He wanted to have fun. He climbed on the motorcycle and pushed a button. It made a loud noise and started to move.

"Tom, stop!" Lily shouted. "It's dangerous!"

But Tom did not listen. He drove the motorcycle on the road, where there were many cars and trucks. He felt happy and fast.

Lily ran after him, but she could not catch up. She was scared and sad. She did not want Tom to get hurt.

Then, she saw a police car with a siren and a light. It was following Tom. It wanted him to stop.

"Tom, please stop!" Lily cried. "The police are here!"

Tom heard Lily and the police. He felt scared and sorry. He did not want to get in trouble. He slowed down and stopped the motorcycle. He got off and waited for the police.

The police officer came and talked to Tom. He was not angry, but he was serious. He told Tom that he did something wrong. He took someone else's motorcycle without asking. He drove it on the road without a helmet or a license. He put himself and others in danger.

Tom felt ashamed and sad. He said he was sorry. He did not mean to do anything bad. He just wanted to have fun.

The police officer nodded and smiled. He said he understood. He said he was glad that Tom was safe and that he stopped. He said he would take the motorcycle back to its owner. He said he would not punish Tom, but he would talk to his parents.

Tom thanked the police officer. He hugged Lily and said he was sorry to her too. He said he would not do it again. He said he learned his lesson.

Lily hugged him back and said she forgave him. She said she loved him. She said they would go home and play with their own toys.

The end.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play and laugh. They are jolly children. But they do not like to share. They want everything for themselves.

One morning, Mom makes toast for breakfast. She puts butter and jam on the toast. She cuts the toast into four pieces. She gives two pieces to Sara and two pieces to Ben.

"Thank you, Mom," Sara and Ben say. They start to eat their toast. They like the toast. It is yummy and warm.

But then, Sara sees that Ben has more jam on his toast. She wants more jam too. She thinks that Ben's toast is better than hers.

"Sara, can I have some of your butter?" Ben asks. He likes butter too.

"No, Ben. This is my butter. You have more jam. You are greedy," Sara says. She is angry.

"Please, Sara. Just a little bit. I will give you some of my jam," Ben says. He is sad.

"No, Ben. Go away. This is my toast. You cannot have it," Sara says. She pushes Ben away.

Ben cries. He does not like to be pushed. He does not like to be called greedy. He does not like to be sad.

Mom hears Ben crying. She comes to the table. She sees Sara and Ben fighting over the toast.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks. She is not happy.

"Sara is mean. She will not share her butter. She has more toast than me," Ben says.

"Ben is greedy. He wants my butter. He has more jam than me," Sara says.

Mom shakes her head. She is disappointed.

"Sara, Ben, you are both wrong. You have the same amount of toast. You have enough butter and jam. You should be grateful and kind. You should share and be jolly. That is what good children do," Mom says.

She takes one piece of toast from Sara and one piece of toast from Ben. She swaps them. She gives Sara a piece of toast with more jam and Ben a piece of toast with more butter.

"There. Now you both have what you want. Can you say sorry to each other and eat your toast nicely?" Mom says.

Sara and Ben look at their toast. They look at each other. They feel sorry. They do not want to fight. They want to be jolly.

"Sorry, Sara. I was greedy. You can have some of my butter," Ben says.

"Sorry, Ben. I was mean. You can have some of my jam," Sara says.

They hug each other. They smile. They eat their toast. They are jolly again.

Mom smiles too. She is proud of Sara and Ben. She is happy. She hugs them too.

"Good children. I love you both. Enjoy your toast," Mom says.

The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with dolls and cars. One day, Anna has a new doll. It has long hair and a pretty dress. Ben likes the doll too. He wants to play with it.

"Can I have your doll?" Ben asks Anna.

"No, it is mine. You have your car," Anna says.

But Ben does not listen. He takes the doll from Anna. He runs away with it. Anna is sad and angry. She cries.

"Give me back my doll!" Anna shouts.

Ben does not stop. He runs to his room. He plays with the doll. He pulls the doll's hair. He makes a knot. He cuts the hair with scissors. He makes the hair short and ugly.

Anna follows Ben. She sees what he did. She is very sad and angry. She screams.

"You are bad! You ruined my doll! I hate you!" Anna says.

Ben is scared. He sees that he did a bad thing. He is sorry. He wants to make Anna happy again.

"I am sorry, Anna. I was wrong. I should not take your doll. I should not cut her hair. I am sorry," Ben says.

He gives the doll back to Anna. He gives her a hug. He gives her a thread. The thread is long and colorful.

"Maybe you can fix your doll's hair with this thread. Maybe you can make her pretty again. I hope you forgive me," Ben says.

Anna is still sad and angry. But she sees that Ben is sorry. She sees that he tries to help. She remembers that he is her friend. She thinks for a while. She takes the thread. She takes the doll. She takes the hug.

"Thank you, Ben. I am still sad, but I forgive you. You are my friend. Maybe we can fix my doll together," Anna says.

They go to Anna's room. They use the thread to make new hair for the doll. They make the hair long and colorful. They make the doll pretty again. They play with the doll and the car. They are happy. They are friends.
